newsitem.title: USA: Pension bond issue studied for Iowa - treasurer.
newsitem.headline: Pension bond issue studied for Iowa - treasurer.

text.p: - Iowa Treasurer Michael Fitzgerald said Wednesday the state was studying the possibility of a taxable bond issue to fund future pension liabilities.

He said a study was currently underway on switching all or some of the state's $10 billion pension fund to a defined contribution system that would enable individual employees to determine the investment of their retirement earnings.
Fitzgerald said a defined contribution system would also give employees the advantage of portability of their retirement savings.

However, switching to such a system could require the funding of future pension liabilities, which he pegged at about $1 billion for Iowa's fund covering state employees and teachers. A taxable bond issue is one way to raise those funds, he added.
The defined contribution study is expected to be completed this year and the legislature is scheduled to review pension laws next year, Fitzgerald said.
Until then, Fitzgerald said he was following proposals in Michigan and New Jersey to issue pension bonds.
"For us, it's not until next year at the earliest," he added.
